warning: Declared symptoms are the CLAIMS someone brings in. Each one is the story that sounds most convincing and is most often wrong. The graph answers CONFIRMED, CONTRADICTED or UNKNOWN from saved evidence only, and never proposes a change to any live setting or names any provider.

declarations.declared: HTTPS works for small messages and fails for large ones, so the path MTU must be low.
declarations.tempting: the observed local interface MTU is the culprit
declarations.why_tempting: there is a real number on the router and it looks like an answer

declarations.declared: No packet-too-big has ever been seen, so there is no size limit.
declarations.tempting: absence of evidence treated as evidence of absence
declarations.why_tempting: RFC 1191 filtering means the error usually never arrives at all

declarations.declared: Uploads fail above a certain size, so the packet size is wrong.
declarations.tempting: an HTTP body limit read as a network limit
declarations.why_tempting: the number is right there in the response, in bytes

declarations.declared: A handful of probes is enough to decide this.
declarations.tempting: a confident verdict from two observations
declarations.why_tempting: two data points always draw a line

declarations.declared: Large transfers stall, so a path size limit is the cause.
declarations.why_tempting: size and stall correlate more often than size and a real limit

declarations.declared: The router's reported MTU is this path's limit.
declarations.tempting: a local number promoted to a path fact
declarations.why_tempting: it came from a router and routers are about paths
